resolved_items.item: Whether the AEMeasurable domain makes the Lean statement genuinely stronger than the source
resolved_items.resolution: It does not. Although AEMeasurable admits representatives that are not pointwise measurable, the conclusion depends only on the resulting probability law. Every Lean instance is covered by the source identity applied to the identity random variable on that law.
resolved_items.primary_evidence: The source on PDF page 3 states the complement identity for an arbitrary real random variable. D003 defines distribution as Measure.map X μ; D001 and D002 evaluate that law on Iic and Ioi; D004 gives AEMeasurable; and distribution_isProbabilityMeasure establishes the mapped law is a probability measure.

resolved_items.item: Whether source implies Lean by applying the source to the identity random variable on the pushforward law
resolved_items.resolution: Yes. For a Lean instance let ν=Measure.map X μ. The identity on Borel Real is a measurable real random variable on (Real,ν), so the source gives ν(Ioi t)=1-ν(Iic t), exactly the Lean conclusion.
resolved_items.primary_evidence: PDF page 3 gives P{X>t}=1-F_X(t) with F_X(t)=P{X≤t}. D017 fixes Borel Real, D024 and D025 fix Iic/Ioi, and D001-D003 identify the target sides as the corresponding masses under ν.

resolved_items.resolution: The target is a nonvacuous law-level complement identity. Both sides evaluate the same mapped probability law on complementary intervals; ordinary measurable constant functions satisfy the premises.
resolved_items.primary_evidence: D001-D004 and D024-D026 fix the measure, interval, map, and AEMeasurable semantics; IsProbabilityMeasure and distribution_isProbabilityMeasure provide normalization.

lean_implies_source.reasoning: A source real random variable is measurable and hence AEMeasurable; the mapped-law masses on Ioi and Iic have exactly the strict-upper and inclusive-lower source meanings.

source_implies_lean.reasoning: For any Lean instance its mapped distribution is a probability measure on Borel Real. Applying the source identity to the measurable identity random variable on that law yields exactly the target equality.

findings.evidence: The source uses a conventionally measurable random variable while Lean assumes only AEMeasurable, but the conclusion is entirely about Measure.map X μ.
findings.impact: This broadens representatives but not the semantic theorem; the identity variable on the mapped law proves every instance.

rationale: The target is the complement identity for the probability law ν=map X μ, not a literal preimage-event assertion retaining extra representative information. The source applies to the identity random variable on every real probability law, including ν, and measurable source variables are Lean-admissible. Both implications hold, so the classification is faithful-equivalent.
